_comment: Owner settings for crash_bot.py. monthly_usd = total new money per month AFTER the debt is gone (split across the two legs below). start = first month the rule runs. debt.balance_sgd = what is left to repay; update it (and as_of) whenever you pay some off. satellite = the stocks you hold on conviction: thesis is printed every day; bear_case is printed daily too (the other side, so you never only hear the bull story); breaks_if is what would make you sell (edit both in your own words; add the third company the same way).

AMZN.name: Amazon
thesis: AWS: the first and the best cloud — nobody builds datacenters like Amazon
AI compute: AWS datacenters and Trainium chips run frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI; Bedrock sells their models to every AWS customer
Robotics: investing heavily, robots rolling out across its warehouses — the best at datacenters AND robotics
Camillo: the 'ultimate beneficiary' of AI's next wave (efficiency + automation) — the essential infrastructure layer
Camillo: AI lifts several businesses at once — AWS, ads (better targeting), Trainium chips as an alternative to Nvidia
Camillo: Amazon reportedly owns ~15% of Anthropic — at a $1–2T Anthropic that stake alone dwarfs its ~$200B AI capex
Camillo: the market fears the capex; he thinks Amazon is spending too LITTLE on AI
breaks_if: AWS growth trails Azure and Google Cloud for 4+ quarters in a row
Anthropic or OpenAI move their main compute off AWS
robotics spend never shows up as better retail margins
free cash flow stays deeply negative (reported ≈−$42B over 12 months on ~$220B capex) with no AWS acceleration to show for it

ANT.name: Anthropic
thesis: huge runway: fewer than 1% of Fortune 500 companies pay it >$1M/month (your figure, unverified)
more of corporate America will inevitably pay for the AI efficiency gains
breaks_if: revenue growth slows sharply for 2+ quarters
big enterprise customers switch to a rival model
a rival model is clearly better for a year or more
bear_case: the 'best model' lead changes hands every few months (OpenAI, Google), and cheap open-weight models push prices down
huge compute bills — tens of billions committed to Google, Amazon, Microsoft; not expected profitable until ~2028, so more cash burn and possible new shares
a big slice of revenue reportedly comes from a few customers (coding tools like Cursor, GitHub Copilot)
fresh AI IPO: high price vs revenue, big swings; insider lockup likely ends ~May 2027 (selling pressure)
public benefit company: its trust can put safety ahead of shareholders
overlaps your Amazon bet — Amazon owns a big stake and earns from it through AWS
